title: Rules FAQ: What’s the deal with paid arrangements? Why can’t I make them here? Where do I go?

posts.author: Ms Littlefish
posts.body:
Hi RMW!
Reminder!
The
Project Recruitment
,
Resource Requests
,
JS Plugin Requests
, and
Resource Workshops
sections are for free work and skill trades only.
The only sections where paid offers and requests will be approved are
Classifieds-Offers
and
Classifieds-Requests.
Paid listings made outside of these sections will be moved and placed in the appropriate queue for approval.
If you are new to the forum, this section is permission-locked and will become available when you earn the
regular rank
at 30 posts. Posting history is reviewed by moderation when seeking paid agreements for the first time.
This is a disappointment to many, but our main security against theft and other types of conflict in these sections is deciding who we approve threads for in the first place.
You may in fact ask…
Q:  OK, but why?
A: Individuals with no interest in RPG Maker signed up to post paid advertisements in the section.
The most common problem that arose from this was irrelevant listings, but there were also a number of ghosted accounts that never delivered and stole any deposits that were collected.
Reviewing post history helps us identify that the member uses RPG Maker and has at least a
little
interest in the community.
While disinterest in RPG Maker is not a
guarantee
for problems, this website is above all else a RPG Maker community. Not a freelance marketplace. Not a platform to run a business. Not a general game dev forum.
We also use posting history to gauge how one might conduct themselves in a paid arrangement.
Q: I can see the importance for offers, but why requests too?
A: Requesters have also contributed to many dispute issues over the years, including refusal to pay a previously agreed rate and asset theft.
Making requests viewable would also allow those same offers mentioned above able to bypass any checks. Additionally, undiscovered duplicates of accounts previously banned from Classifieds or banned from the entire forum would be able to view and take up requests.
If your next question is, “Does that really happen?” The answer is…Yes. Not super recently. But. It definitely has occurred more than once and with some frequency before the permissions were changed.
Q: That still seems a bit unfair, I would never steal commission work or refuse to pay what I previously agreed to pay.
A: I 100% believe you. Asset thievery and malicious haggling are not the norms, but screening post history for new requesters provides many of the same clues as to how one might conduct themselves in a paid exchange.
30 posts feels like a lot for a brand new member. But, if you introduce yourself, make a place to start sharing your project, and get involved in other RPG Maker discussions the time will pass quickly. You may even find a little familiarity with the community beneficial.
Q: Will this ever change?
A: Absolutely not off the table!
It is an honest and fair assessment that the current permissions are a story of “a few bad apples spoil the whole bunch.” It’s undeniable that’s what happened here.
It has been difficult to balance concepts that are more fair with keeping it both easy to understand and within the scope of a text-based forum with a volunteer moderation team. But, it has been a fairly frequent topic of discussion over the years.
Basically. The current setup has not yet proven to be so
horribly
broken despite its clear shortcomings, but we actually do consider how imperfect it is.
In conclusion…
If finding commissions within the RPG Maker community is not something you particularly care about
or
if the minimal recourse options worry you—use Fiverr. Or, whatever is popular these days?
If you
do
like the idea of working with the RPG Maker community, we’ll just have to hang out and get to know each other a little bit first.

This is a public
copy
of the Classifieds-Requests rules so new members without the
regular rank
can refer to them before gaining permissions and posting. Reminder that paid requests are
not
to be posted in this section and must be made in the
Classifieds-Requests
section.
Classifieds-Requests Rules
(Last Update: August 22nd, 2024)
​
Threads posted in the Classifieds-Requests board
will enter a moderation queue
and will not appear until it is accepted by a moderator. Threads will be accepted or denied based on how well they meet the rules and guidelines. Give at least 72 hours before inquiring about the state of your thread and address all concerns with a moderator.
When posting in the Classifieds- Requests boards, you are expected to read, understand, and meet the minimum requirements.
Remember
All general rules apply.
[rmod]KOMODO, moderators, and RMW are not responsible for maintaining an agreement or resolving breaches of an agreement. [/rmod]
Though, if you have proof someone has breached an agreement, staff may be able to take moderation action (thread lock, suspension, section ban, account ban, etc)
What is this board for?
​
This is where you can offer
money
for resources or services needed to complete your RPG Maker projects.
If you would like to acquire resources or services for free - use
Resource Requests
or
JS Plugin Requests
respectively​
If you would like to find long term collaborators for free or a skill trade - use
Project Recruitment
​
If you would like to find free workshops available for requests - use
Resource Workshops
​
Requirements to Open a New Thread
​
You may only request resources for a game engine published by KOMODO
-
no other game engines are permitted.
Your post must follow the
TAGGING GUIDE
.
Include a
clear and full
description of what you need, including reference images and/or mockups when needed. The more info, the more likely your request is to be filled.
Only request edits of resources or maps to be made of tiles that you are legally allowed to use and edit.
Your post must indicate you are willing and able to pay.
You must also indicate
how
you will pay (PayPal, Venmo, etc). You
may
ask for a quote or estimate. You
may
ask for responders to provide their rate. But, if you
do
have a set budget, note this. Do not say your budget is “unlimited” unless you actually have unlimited funds.
This board is only for direct and timely cash payments.
Offering a copy of your game, payment after a game release, profit shares, or royalties are not permitted.
In this section, we
do
allow requests that aren't PG-13. However, all public postings, discussions, and uploads must be appropriate for a PG-13 audience. Anything R18+ must be discussed privately.
You are also responsible for making good choices when accepting a R18+ offer.
READ THIS BEFORE ACCEPTING AN OFFER
​
Do not assume there is an agreement until you have it in writing.
Do not accept an offer unless you are certain the member can provide the work at the desired quality, at a price you are willing to pay, and can accept payment via your preferred platform.
Communicate via PM (off-site communications cannot be moderated in the event of a dispute).
If you cannot meet your commitment, let the other person know, and negotiate compensation (i.e partial payment for the work completed or a non-refund on any deposit).
If you cannot resolve a dispute, add a moderator to the conversation.
Conduct yourself honestly and professionally.

copy
of the Classifieds-Offers rules so new members without the
regular rank
can refer to them before gaining permissions and posting. Reminder that paid offers are
not
to be posted in this section and must be made in the
Classifieds-Offers
section.
Classifieds-Offers Rules
(Last Update: August 22nd, 2024)
​
Threads posted in the Classifieds-Offers board
will enter a moderation queue
and will not appear until it is accepted by a moderator. Threads will be accepted or denied based on how well they meet the rules and guidelines. Give at least 72 hours before inquiring about the state of your thread and address all concerns with a moderator.
When posting in the Classifieds-Offers boards, you are expected to read, understand, and meet the minimum requirements.
Remember
All general rules apply.
[rmod]KOMODO, moderators, and RMW are not responsible for maintaining an agreement or resolving breaches of an agreement. [/rmod]
Though, if you have proof someone has breached an agreement, staff may be able to take moderation action (thread lock, suspension, section ban, account ban, etc)
You must own the engine for which you are offering resources.
If your resources can be used in any engine, you must own at least one engine. If deemed necessary, proof of purchase will be requested.
What is this board for?
​
This is where you can request
money
for resources or services needed to complete another’s RPG Maker projects.
If you would like to fulfill one-off requests for free - use
Resource Requests
or
JS Plugin Requests
respectively​
If you would like to find long term collaborators for free or a skill trade - use
Project Recruitment
​
If you would like to fulfill small requests or services in an on-going fashion and for free - use
Resource Workshops
​
[rmod]This section is for the RPG Maker community only.[/rmod]
​
You
must
be a forum member for at least 1 month
and
have 30 posts.
However, your post history
will
be reviewed. Your thread may be rejected if it appears you are not in any way involved with RPG Maker. Your thread may be rejected if it appears you are spamming low effort comments like “cool game” or bumping off-topic threads to hit the post threshold.
It should be apparent from your posting history that you are here to use and discuss RPG Maker.
Requirements to Open a New Thread
​
You may only offer resources for KOMODO published products
-
no other engines are allowed.
Your post must follow the
TAGGING GUIDE
.
You must showcase a portfolio.
This should consist of examples that indicate your skill, range,
and understanding of the RPG Maker resource requirements.
Only offer edits of resources you are legally allowed to use and are allowed to distribute the edits commercially.
Your post must indicate average/starting prices for your products and/or services.
The exact rate may naturally vary on a set of factors, but do not require your prospective clients to privately message you for a basic price determination.
List your preferred payment platform (PayPal, Venmo, etc).
This board is only for direct and timely cash payments.
Accepting a copy of the game, payment after the game release, a profit share, or a royalty is not permitted.
In this section, we
do
allow offers that aren't PG-13. However, all public postings, discussions, and uploads must be appropriate for a PG-13 audience. Anything R18+ must be discussed privately.
You are also responsible for making good choices when fulfilling a R18+ request.
READ THESE BEFORE ACCEPTING A REQUEST.
​
Do not assume there is an agreement until you have it in writing.
Do not accept a request unless you are certain the member can make the required payment and can send the payment via your preferred transfer platform.
Communicate via PM (off-site communications cannot be moderated in the event of a dispute).
If you cannot meet your commitment, let the other person know, and negotiate compensation (i.e refund of any deposit, etc).
If you cannot resolve a dispute, add a moderator to the conversation.
Conduct yourself honestly and professionally.
AI Usage in Classifieds
​
Generated assets have never been allowed. We are making clear this includes AI. If it is ever discovered that a member is passing off AI-generated assets as their own original hand-made works, in as few words as possible,
you’ll be banned.
The only notable exception is the case where an AI assistant can provide support for a human programmer with tasks such as debugging, etc. Plugins and scripts should still never, ever be generated out of an AI chatbot.
Portfolio Requirements
​
There is an expectation of reasonable quality to open a shop.
You may escalate a moderation decision to an admin if you feel your offering was wrongfully rejected, but the moderation team consists of artists, musicians, and programmers that are collectively able to determine reasonable quality.
Provide working
in-engine
examples whenever necessary to fully demonstrate the offering. This could range from screenshots, videos, to demo games on occasion.
If a demo game is provided, remove any unused materials. If for any reason the demo game needs to be unencrypted, then it must only contain materials that can be distributed under those terms.
When offering Game Artwork
Spoiler
You should have plenty of experience with game artwork (2+ years recommended).
All examples must be created by yourself (no edits for the portfolio).
Your game artwork must show you have a reasonable understanding of lighting, shading, composition, and color theory.
Your game artwork must show you have a reasonable grasp on anatomy and/or backgrounds.
Your game artwork must show you have an understanding of how perspective works.
Your game artwork must show you know how to handle different textures and surfaces.
Your game artwork must have no traces of stray pixels surrounding the line-art.
Hand-drawn sketches must be scanned in, cleaned, and preferably inked/digitally inked (no photographs of artwork).
You may offer edits, but this should not be the draw of your shop and you will need both the rights to edit and to distribute edits commercially.
When offering Pixel Art
Spoiler
First and foremost, you should have plenty of experience in pixel art (1+ years recommended).
All examples must be created by yourself (base templates are allowed, but otherwise no edits or frakensprites for the portfolio)
Your pixel art must show you understand how to color and shade with a limited color palette and how to create shapes and edges with a restricted number of pixels.
Your pixel art must show you know how to handle different textures and surfaces.
Your pixel art must show you understand how perspective works.
There should be no stray pixels surrounding your pixel art.
You may offer edits, but this should not be the draw of your shop and you will need both the rights to edit and to distribute edits commercially.
When offering Other Graphic Artwork
Spoiler
First and foremost, you should have plenty of experience in graphic design (1+ years recommended).
All examples must be created by yourself (no edits of logos, menu assets, windowskins, etc for the portfolio)
Your work must show you have an understanding of how image and graphic composition works in the context of an RPG Maker game.
Your colors must complement each other and should not be fatiguing.
Effects and filters should not replace effective graphic design.
Lettering should be legible and textures/patterns should not be blurry or an inappropriate resolution for the item size.
Only incorporate stock art, patterns, fonts, textures, etc in your graphic design that you have the permission to both use and to distribute commercially.
When offering Mapping
Spoiler
Show images and/or videos of your maps.
Your examples can showcase any tile set you own and in whichever program you create them.
Your maps must show you have a good understanding of how to work with space and create a point of interest.
Your maps should show you know how to balance out clutter, empty space, and be made to the appropriate size.
Your work must contain no errors (height differences in cliffs, perspective issues, auto tile errors, clipped off tiles, and etc.).
Tile styles should not clash and be consistent with each other (i.e. pixel art vs. painted art).
You should know how to tint and light a map without sacrificing details and functionality.
You can only use the tile sets that the commissioner themselves have the right to use.
When offering Music/Audio
Spoiler
First and foremost, you should have plenty of experience in composing + producing music and/or other audio (2+ years recommended).
All examples must be composed by yourself (no edits/remixes allowed for the portfolio).
Your music must show you have an understanding of tonality, rhythm, time, and phrasing.
Your music must show you have a reasonable grasp on melody, harmony, and chord progression.
Your music must show you have a reasonable understanding of mixing audio and setting loop points (the audio must function for game use, it should not be overly muddy, and it should not be difficult to discern the instrument parts from one another).
Your music/audio should be free of clicking, excessive microphone/electrical noise, excessive room noise, excessive background noise, and clipping.
Overuse of pre-rendered audio loops (that you did not create yourself) will be rejected.
You may offer edits, but this should not be the draw of your shop and you will need both the rights to edit and to distribute edits commercially.
When offering Writing
Spoiler
You must provide a sample of your writing skills. This should cover a few scenes.
All examples must be created by yourself (no edits of another’s writing for the portfolio).
Your work must show that you have a good grasp on the English language.
Your samples must feature correct spelling and grammar.
Your samples must prove that you are capable of creating something better than your potential customers.
You are writing for an interactive game. Your samples should be formatted like a screenplay, not a story.
Consider showcasing your scenes directly in the engine. Pairing words with on-screen events and images will convey the script with much greater effect than on the page alone.
You may offer to edit, but this should not be the draw of your shop.
When offering Plugins and/or Scripts
Spoiler
First and foremost, you should have plenty of experience programming in JavaScript and/or Ruby in the context of RPG Maker ( 1+ years recommended).
All examples must be your own work (no edits or compatibility patches for the portfolio).
Your plugins and/or scripts should show you have a reasonable grasp of coding best practices for the languages you are offering services.
You must include a portfolio example for every type of plugin and/or script service you are offering (i.e. if you are offering menu alterations/features, battle systems, etc. you must provide an accessible portfolio entry for each that a prospective client can sample meaningfully).
Your plugins and/or scripts should not be overly reliant on the usage of AI assistance.
You may offer edits and/or compatibility patches
,
but this should not be the draw of your shop and you will need both the rights to edit and to distribute edits commercially.

This is a public
copy
of the Classifieds dispute resolution guide
so new members without the
regular rank
can refer to them before gaining permissions and posting.
[rmod] KOMODO, moderators, and RMW are not responsible for maintaining an agreement or resolving breaches of an agreement. [/rmod]
Classifieds is offered as a courtesy to RMW forum members who are interested in working with each other. That said, Classifieds has always been largely at your own risk.
HOWEVER
.
It is
NOT
acceptable to be commissioned and fail to deliver.
It is
NOT
acceptable to request a commission and fail to make the agreed payment.
If you have proof someone has breached an agreement, staff may be able to take moderation action (thread lock, suspension, section ban, account ban, etc).
[rmod]If you are involved in an active dispute, do not attempt to request new commissions or fulfill new commissions until it is fully resolved. [/rmod]
Impacted threads will be locked and hidden until your dispute is resolved. Even if your dispute is resolved agreeably, moderation action may still be needed depending on the circumstances.
If your dispute goes unresolved, your threads will be deleted and you will have access to the section permanently revoked.
Do not assume there is an agreement until you have it in writing.
There is no agreement without a written confirmation. Do not jump the gun. Both sides need to understand the totality of the work order and what the expectations are for delivery time and pricing. Be aware that discussing these factors can result in either side recognizing they are not well matched.
Only when it is written and exceedingly clear to start the exchange, should any deposit funds be traded and any work on the order begin.
Do not accept an offer unless you are certain the member can provide the work at the desired quality, at a price you are willing to pay, and that they can accept the payment via your preferred transfer platform
.
Do your homework. Ask for samples, particularly ones that meet the specifications you are requesting. Search for reviews. Do others recommend working with them? Do not make an agreement unless you are confident they have the skills to provide what you need at your desired quality and desired price. Do
not
accept an offer if you cannot pay their rate and/or use their preferred payment platform.
Do not accept a request unless you are certain the member can make the required payment and can send the payment via your preferred transfer platform.
Before offering to fulfill a request, make sure the person understands what you will be doing, how much that will cost, how long that will take, and what payment method you require. Do
not
offer to complete a request unless you’re confident the requester has understood the proper expectations, can pay your rate, and can transfer it using a preferred payment method.
Communicate via PM (off-site communications cannot be moderated in the event of a dispute).
Once an agreement has been reached conduct
ALL
your communication via PM. Do not take it to email, Discord, social media, or to another forum. If a dispute arises, THIS IS YOUR EVIDENCE. What happens outside the forum stays there. We will not consider anything that happens outside the forum. Do not delete your PMs in an effort to prevent staff from reviewing. That will look bad.
If you cannot resolve a dispute, add a moderator to the conversation.
Keep communication open. Failing to respond could be seen as the first sign of abandoning obligation. If you have provided your half of the deal and the other party has gone silent without communicating schedule changes, PM a mod
(Ms Littlefish is the primary Classifieds contact)
and explain the situation. We will intervene on your behalf and take action based on the outcome.
Within reason, it is OK to cancel. It is NOT OK to fail to deliver.
If either party has decided the deal is not going to work out as expected, it's okay to cancel the agreement as long as no payment has been made and no resources have been handed over. Notify the other party ASAP. Do not leave them in the dark. If resources
HAVE
been provided or payment
HAS
been made, you are obligated to live up to your end of the bargain. If you do not, it is expected that you refund any deposits or that you will not use any resources that have been delivered.
Conduct yourself honestly and professionally.
Hopefully this does not warrant too much explanation. This is not a place to play games or make a half-hearted effort at something. If you do not act with integrity or make an effort to resolve any issues that might occur, you will be removed from the section.
